text:
incident-bot: 🔔 PD-23911 triggered — Suncrest (private VPC) high 5xx rate via customer NLB (us-west-2). target group tg-suncrest-ml-3 showing >90% unhealthy, pagered eng-sre oncall.
maria: oncall here, looking — can someone grab last 10m error rate and which dedicated pool is serving? @sophie any customer-side notes?
sophie: customer says ~30% of requests are failing with 502/504s, production traffic impacted. reported first seen ~13:12 UTC, several tenants report degraded model responses.
trent: I'm seeing NLB healthchecks failing to targets. health path /health returns 504 from backends. target IPs are responding slowly and conntrack on tenant hosts is near limit (10.0.5.0/24). possible egress/NAT exhaustion + sticky session pressure.
maria: ok — immediate plan: 1) remove obviously unhealthy targets from TG, 2) open healthcheck SG to NLB health IPs, 3) shift a portion of DNS weight to fallback dedicated pool in us-east-1. I'll run step 1 now.
maria: exec (paste):
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:1111111:targetgroup/tg-suncrest-ml-3/aaaaaa --targets Id=i-0abcd1234 Id=i-0dcba4321
```
maria: removed 3 targets from tg-suncrest-ml-3 — immediate error rate dropped to ~18% from 90% (still high). adding monitoring window.
trent: i'm temporarily adding NLB healthcheck CIDR to SG (allow from 10.0.0.0/8 for healthchecks) and increasing conntrack on host pool as short-term. will keep tight TTL.
sophie: customer confirms partial recovery, still seeing spikes under heavy batch requests. they're throttling retries but want us to fix permanently.
maria: next: DNS weight shift. preparing Route53 change to move 30% traffic to fallback pool in us-east-1 (suncrest-fallback-ml). will do controlled 10/20/30 over 10m steps.
raj: i'm taking over oncall for the next 60m — monitoring and will execute the DNS roll forward if metrics stable. maria, leave me the playbook notes.
maria: notes: why happened: tenant hosts hit NAT conntrack + sticky sessions caused uneven load; NLB healthchecks timed out -> cascade. temporary mitigations applied: deregister unhealthy targets, open health SG, increase conntrack, route53 weighted shift.
trent: scheduling infra change to scale NAT gateway/egress pool for Suncrest dedicated VPC. also will add preflight healthcheck queue shard to reduce per-host pressure.
lee: assigning RCA owner -> lee will own postmortem and long-term mitigation (autoscale NAT, healthcheck backoff, client-side retry guidance).
sophie: looping in AM for customer update (we'll send interim note: mitigations applied, monitoring ongoing, next update in 30m).
raj: monitoring graphs (5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, target health counts). current 5xx trending down to 6% after steps. will escalate back if >10%.
maria: adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress (follow section "NLB health + conntrack") — also tagging incident in tracker PD-23911.
trent: leaving SG change open for 45m then revert if stable.
raj: handing off final watch to lee for RCA timeline. i'll add action items to the incident doc.
lee: got it — will own RCA & followups. scheduled postmortem meeting tomorrow 1600 UTC.
sophie: customer update sent: "we see improvement; engineering is monitoring and will provide an RCA." :+1:
maria: closing operational loop here — will remain in thread for logs if needed. great teamwork. :white_check_mark:
